title: The tongue and taste
examples: How do taste buds actually work?
Is it true that we can only taste five things?
What is umami and where do we find it?

explain.say: Today we are learning about your tongue and how you taste food.
Taste buds are tiny sensors found all over your tongue.

draw.text: Taste Buds: Small sensors on the tongue

explain.say: The five basic tastes are sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and umami.

draw.text: Five Tastes: Sweet, Salty, Sour, Bitter, Umami

explain.say: Sweet tastes are often found in fruits and desserts you enjoy.

draw.text: Sweet: Found in fruit and sugar

explain.say: Salty tastes come from minerals, such as the salt we add to food.
Umami is a savory taste often found in things like ripe tomatoes or mushrooms.

faq.q: Can I only taste these five things?
faq.a: No, you can taste many things beyond these five basic tastes. Your sense of smell also plays a very important role in what you taste.
asks: Are there other tastes besides the five?
Do I need my nose to taste well?

faq.a: Yes, your taste buds can become less sensitive over time. This is why sometimes food tastes different when you are sick.
asks: Can my taste buds wear out?
Why does food taste funny when I have a cold?

faq.a: Sour taste is just an indicator of acidity in food. Foods like lemons are naturally sour, but some sour foods are healthy.
asks: What causes food to taste sour?

faq.a: It is difficult to say which taste is the strongest. Everyone's taste sensitivity can be different from person to person.
asks: Is bitter taste stronger than sweet?
Does one taste beat the others?

faq.a: Taste buds contain receptors that react when chemicals from food touch them. These receptors send signals to your brain to tell you the taste.
asks: What is the job of a taste bud?
How do I know if something is sweet?

facts: Taste buds are located on the surface of the tongue.
The five basic tastes recognized are sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and umami.
Taste is a combination of taste and smell.
Umami is often described as a savory or meaty flavor.

quiz.say: If you eat a ripe banana, which taste are you mostly experiencing?
quiz.why: Bananas are high in natural sugars, which register as sweet.

wrong.1: Salty tastes come from minerals like salt, not fruit.
wrong.2: Sour tastes are usually associated with high acidity, like lemons.
wrong.3: Bitter tastes are often found in things like coffee or certain leaves.

quiz.say: Which taste is associated with the savory flavor found in aged cheese?
quiz.why: Umami is the savory taste, often linked to aged foods and mushrooms.

wrong.1: Sweet is related to sugars, which cheese does not contain.
wrong.2: While cheese is often salted, the deep savory note is umami.
wrong.3: Sourness comes from acids, which is a different flavor profile.

quiz.say: When you taste a lemon, you are mainly detecting which taste?
quiz.why: Lemons are acidic, and that acidity registers as a sour taste.

wrong.0: Sweetness comes from sugars, which lemons do not contain.
wrong.1: Umami is a deep savory taste, not the sharp tang of citrus.
wrong.3: Salty requires dissolved minerals, which lemons lack.
